beats.say: Name a pattern. Now defend it.
A staff answer knows the problem each pattern solves. And what it costs.
beats.label: The staff answer
beats.head: What it solves, what it costs

beats.say: Four patterns come up most: Lambda and Kappa, medallion layers, the outbox, and data mesh.
beats.label: Track 15 · Architecture patterns

check.prompt: What is the main cost of the Lambda architecture?
options: Two code paths to keep in step
check.why: Lambda has a batch path and a stream path, so you write and fix the logic twice.

beats.say: First: batch, stream, or both?
Lambda runs two paths. A fast stream for now, and a batch for the correct result.
beats.label: Lambda
beats.head: Two paths: fast and correct

beats.say: The cost: you write the same logic twice, and keep both in step.
beats.label: Its cost
beats.head: The same logic, twice

beats.say: Kappa keeps only the stream. To fix history, you replay the log.
beats.label: Kappa
beats.head: One path. Replay to fix.

check.prompt: Which layer keeps the raw data, as it arrived?
check.why: Bronze is raw. Silver is clean. Gold is ready for the business.

beats.say: Second: bronze, silver, gold.
Bronze is the raw data, as it arrived. Silver is clean. Gold is ready for the business.
beats.label: Three layers

beats.say: Keep bronze unchanged. Then you can rebuild silver and gold at any time.
beats.label: Why it works
beats.head: Raw data lets you rebuild

beats.say: Third: save to the database, and publish an event.
If you do the two steps apart, one can fail. Then the systems disagree.
beats.label: The problem
beats.head: Two writes can disagree

beats.say: So write the event to an outbox table, in the same transaction.
beats.label: The outbox
beats.head: One transaction, two rows

beats.say: A separate process reads the outbox and publishes. Nothing is lost.
beats.label: Then
beats.head: Publish from the outbox

beats.say: Last: who owns the data?
In a data mesh, each domain team owns its data as a product.
beats.label: Data mesh
beats.head: Each domain owns its data

beats.say: It fits a large company. For a small team, it is too much overhead. Say no.
beats.label: When to say no
beats.head: Small team? Say no.

beats.say: Quick recap of the patterns.
Lambda costs two code paths. Keep bronze raw. And use an outbox for two writes.
beats.label: Architecture patterns

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
